gloss: kagura; sacred Shinto music and dance

definitions.gloss: kagura, sacred Shinto music and dance
definitions.explanation: A form of ritual music and dance performed to honor and entertain the Shinto gods (kami). One of Japan's oldest performing arts, originating in myths about the goddess Ame no Uzume dancing to lure Amaterasu out of a cave. Performed at shrines during festivals.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{神楽|かぐら}が{奉納|ほうのう}された。
examples.english: Kagura was performed as an offering at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {秋祭|あきまつ}りでは{毎年|まいとし}{地元|じもと}の{人|ひと}たちが{神楽|かぐら}を{舞|ま}う。
examples.english: At the autumn festival, local people perform kagura dances every year.

examples.japanese: {神楽|かぐら}の{起源|きげん}は、{天照大神|あまてらすおおみかみ}が{天|あま}の{岩戸|いわと}に{隠|かく}れた{際|さい}に{天宇受売命|あめのうずめのみこと}が{踊|おど}ったことにあるとされる。
examples.english: The origin of kagura is said to lie in the dance performed by Ame no Uzume when Amaterasu hid in the cave of heaven.

notes:
USAGE:
There are two main types: {御|み}{神楽|かぐら} (court kagura performed at the imperial palace) and {里|さと}{神楽|かぐら} (folk kagura performed at local shrines). Folk kagura varies greatly by region and is a living tradition still performed at festivals throughout Japan.

ETYMOLOGY:
Believed to derive from {神|かみ}{座|くら} (seat of the gods), referring to the sacred space where the gods gather to be entertained.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神楽|かぐら}を{舞|ま}う: to perform a kagura dance
- {神楽|かぐら}を{奉納|ほうのう}する: to offer/dedicate a kagura performance
- {神楽|かぐら}{殿|でん}: kagura hall (at a shrine)
- {神楽|かぐら}{面|めん}: kagura mask
